steps.title: Keep all reagents on ice
steps.instruction: Maintain all components and reaction tubes on ice (or at 4 °C) throughout the procedure.

steps.title: Prepare template RNA
steps.instruction: Gently thaw template RNA on ice. Use ≤ 100 ng total RNA per 20 µL reverse‑transcription (RT) reaction and adjust each sample to a similar concentration with nuclease‑free water so that the same amount of RNA is used across all panels.

steps.title: Reverse‑transcribe RNA
steps.instruction: Incubate the RT reaction at 42 °C for 30 min (00:30:00).

steps.title: Keep cDNA on ice or store
steps.instruction: After incubation, keep the undiluted cDNA reactions on ice until the real‑time PCR assembly, or store at –20 °C for up to three days if desired.

steps.title: Assemble real‑time PCR plate
steps.instruction: In the sealed bag supplied, add the required qPCR reagents to the plate without removing the bag until you are ready to run the assay. Keep all reagents on ice (or at 4 °C) during set‑up. Include a melt‑curve analysis step as recommended by your qPCR instrument’s manual.

steps.title: Spin plate briefly
steps.instruction: Centrifuge the plate for 30 s at 200 × g in a suitable plate centrifuge (00:00:30).

steps.title: Run real‑time PCR
steps.instruction: Perform real‑time PCR using the cycling parameters listed in Table 3 of the kit manual, ensuring exact adherence to the program. Add the melt‑curve module as described by the instrument manufacturer.

steps.title: Collect raw Ct values
steps.instruction: After the run, collect raw Ct (Cp or Cq) values with the instrument software. Do not use auto‑Ct; set the fluorescence threshold manually to one‑tenth of the average maximal fluorescence value.

steps.title: Export data to Excel
steps.instruction: Export the Ct data as an Excel file for downstream analysis.

steps.title: Heat‑inactivate reverse transcriptase
steps.instruction: Heat the completed RT reactions at 90 °C for 5 min (00:05:00) to inactivate the enzyme.

steps.title: Verify control wells
steps.instruction: Check that Ct values in inter‑plate calibrator wells (E12/F12 and G12/H12) are approximately equal, and that spike‑control wells (A12/B12 and C12/D12) also give similar Ct values. Consistent duplicates indicate low pipetting error.

steps.title: Interpret miRNA results
steps.instruction: Consider a Ct < 36 as a positive detection and Ct > 36 as negative. Treat Ct values of 34‑35 with caution, as they approach the assay’s limit of detection.
